subject: Post-demo: recommended inference slate, benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ari Hoffman <ari@stratify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended inference slate, benchmarks & next steps

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for joining the call today. Attached is a concise package with the recommended inference slate, basic benchmarks we ran against your sample prompt set, and a prompt pack you can use to validate outputs during the pilot (see attachments and Drive link below).

High-level recommended shortlist (for your evaluation sprint):

1) Redwood-Opt-13B (high-quality, moderate cost)
   - Strength: best blind-qa and instruction-following on your sample prompts (lowest error on extraction tasks).
   - Observed median p95 latency (128-token reply): ~98 ms on a shared 80GB GPU instance.
   - Unit cost: ~$0.80 per 1k output tokens (hosted); predictable in Dedicated.

2) Mistral-7B-Inst (quantized, cost-balanced)
   - Strength: strong quality for conversational flows, excellent throughput for short responses.
   - Observed median p95 latency (128-token reply): ~62 ms quantized on Ampere X; ~0.32 USD per 1k output tokens.
   - Good candidate for early pilot to reduce spend.

3) Redwood-Edge-3B (compact, latency/cost optimized)
   - Strength: lowest cost and fastest tail latency for short completions; acceptable for templated responses and reranking.
   - Observed median p95 latency (64-token reply): ~28 ms; ~0.08 USD per 1k output tokens.

Rationale notes:
- We prioritized models that cover the three operational tradeoffs you flagged on the call: (1) quality for extraction/QA, (2) cost per active user at scale, and (3) tail-latency for interactive workflows.
- The recommended path is: run parallel 2-week evals of Redwood-Opt-13B and Mistral-7B on your top 150 prompt variants, measure quality delta on your labeled set, and then gate the pilot on the crossover point where quality lift justifies cost.

Attached / linked materials:
- stratify_prompt_pack_v1.zip (150 prompt variants + expected outputs)
- q3_inference_benchmarks.csv (raw run metrics vs your sample prompts)
- pilot_estimate_cost_model.xlsx (cost scenarios for 50k / 200k monthly users)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_prompt-pack-stratify

Proposed next steps (quick wins):
- Confirm which 150 prompts to include in the sprint (we preselected a balanced 50/50 split of QA vs conversational).
- We’ll provision a dedicated sandbox project for you with 48-hour demo tokens and a short Canary routing policy.
- Schedule 30-min sync next Tue to review initial benchmark results and align on acceptance criteria for hallucination thresholds.

If that plan looks good, I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering to scope pilot provisioning and provide a firm estimate for Dedicated capacity.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Hi Ari — quick answers to your bullets, with empirical numbers from the Sprint bench we ran against your sample set. See attached CSV for raw data.

1) Hallucination metrics
   - Method: we ran 150 labeled prompts (your pack) and measured factuality against the labeled ground truth.
   - Results (aggregate): Redwood-Opt-13B: hallucination rate 4.6% on extractions; Mistral-7B-Inst: 6.9%; Redwood-Edge-3B: 12.4%.
   - Note: hallucination severity is higher on long-form reasoning prompts; we recommend the Opt-13B for any tasks requiring strict fidelity.

2) Data retention & logs
   - Sandbox default retention: 30 days. Logs can be forwarded to your S3 (encrypted) during pilot; we can add a non-retention mode for PII-sensitive flows.
   - For Dedicated / Private: retention and log routing are customer-configurable (KMS/HSM supported).

3) SLA & failover
   - Dedicated baseline SLOs: p95 latency target for 128-token replies = 110 ms; availability SLA = 99.95% (region-dependent).
   - Fallback options: automatic routing to compatible quantized variants (e.g., Opt-13B -> Opt-13B-quant or Mistral-7B) with graceful degradation policy.

4) Cost estimate (50k MAU scenario)
   - Assumptions: 120 generated tokens / session, 1.8 sessions / MAU / day, 22 business days for peak cost calc.
   - Run math (approx): Opt-13B hosted -> ~$0.80 per 1k tokens -> ~ $0.80 * (50,000 * 1.8 * 120 / 1000) * 22 ≈ $190k / month (peak).
   - Mistral-7B-Inst (quantized) -> ~$0.32 per 1k -> ~ $76k / month (peak).
   - Redwood-Edge-3B -> ~$0.08 per 1k -> ~ $19k / month (peak).
   - Dedicated reserved capacity pricing will reduce unit cost by ~20-40% depending on commit and autoscaling profile. We included scenarios in pilot_estimate_cost_model.xlsx.

5) Compliance / SOC2 evidence
   - We can provide SOC2 Type II report and a short evidence pack for procurement. I’ll share the internal package link after I get a procurement contact.

If helpful, we can run a short A/B shortlist during the first week of the pilot and hold a quality review with your SME team on day 10.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
